clue.text: Almost bid sleep farewell

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: nursery talk for sleep, as in 'off to bye-byes'

explanation.surface: Someone nearly says goodnight to sleep itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bid farewell' reads as one phrase, but 'bid' only joins; the child's word for sleep loses its last letter to give BYE-BYE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bye-bye is an informal parting word, used exactly as one would say goodbye.

clue.text: You are not finished in time

indicators.note: something not finished stops short, so the phrase drops its last letter

parts.note: ye is the archaic you, followed by are

explanation.surface: Someone is told they have run out of time before completing a task.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is a standard measured period, so it serves as an example of a length of time.

clue.text: Bank least prepared for high growth

indicators.note: something prepared has been worked up into a new form, so these letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: A financial institution is caught unready for a period of rapid economic expansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High growth' sounds like economics, but it is Jack's towering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The beanstalk in the fairy tale grows up into the sky, a plant of famously great height.

clue.text: One hug should be sufficient

indicators.note: the words are told what they ought to become, inviting their letters to be remade

explanation.surface: A single embrace ought to satisfy anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Enough and sufficient are synonyms, both meaning as much as is required.

clue.text: Hear a couple of stories and have a drink

indicators.note: hearing points to what is spoken, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: two kinds of story, a lie and a tale, said together

explanation.surface: An evening at the pub: listening to anecdotes over a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: Light ale is a pale bottled beer, so it is one kind of alcoholic drink served in pubs.

clue.text: Pension qualification extended by dilatory minister

parts.note: surface reading: the years of work that earn a pension
setter's reading: a slow clergyman draws out the duration of his church worship

explanation.surface: A civil servant's slowness boosts their pension entitlement.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed grid has a T where the H belongs. A minister in church leads a service, and a dilatory one makes it long.
explanation.definitionFit: Pension rights often depend on how many years someone has worked for an employer.

clue.text: Have a regular date to do stage production at the end of July

indicators.note: a production remakes material into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
only the closing letter of the month is wanted

explanation.surface: A theatre company plans a summer show and fixes a booking for the end of July.
explanation.definitionFit: To go steady is an idiom for dating one partner exclusively on a regular basis.

clue.text: Material that's precious found with diamonds

parts.note: precious in the sense of affectedly dainty

explanation.surface: A luxurious fabric is set with gemstones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precious' suggests jewels beside diamonds, but here it means twee, overly cute.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweed is a rough woollen cloth, so it is a kind of fabric or material.

clue.text: The French people submit — it's awful

parts.note: to table a motion is to put it forward

explanation.surface: A complaint that the French surrendering is dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamentable means deplorably bad, worthy of grief, so it matches awful closely.

clue.text: A biscuit or a half roll dunked in burgundy

indicators.note: dunked things go inside a liquid, so these letters sit within the wine

parts.note: Mâcon is a Burgundy wine; this is its first part

indicators.note: only half the word is kept, so two of its four letters go

parts.note: only its first half is kept

explanation.surface: At teatime someone dunks a biscuit or bread roll in red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Mâcon is a wine from southern Burgundy, the region often just called burgundy in lower case for its wines.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaroon is a small almond biscuit, sweet and chewy.

clue.text: Erotic, like a Turkish bath?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: full of hot vapour

explanation.walkthrough: A Turkish bath is a steam room, so the literal sense is full of steam.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes both sexually charged scenes and rooms thick with hot vapour.

clue.text: Take a deep breath before walking on — it's a skill acquired by musicians

parts.note: a sigh is a long audible breath

explanation.surface: A performer composes themselves before stepping out on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Players learn to perform unseen notation at first glance, a technique taught to instrumentalists.

clue.text: A missing London woman is musical

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: a lady from Mayfair, a smart district of London

explanation.surface: A woman from London has disappeared, which is a song-and-dance matter.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayfair is an upmarket area of central London; drop its A.
explanation.definitionFit: My Fair Lady is a famous stage show by Lerner and Loewe, adapted from Pygmalion.

clue.text: Los Angeles hosts 2 contracted stars

indicators.note: a host holds guests within, so these letters go inside
contracted means shortened, so the word is cut to an abbreviation

explanation.surface: Hollywood plays host to celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' points to the solution at 2 down, abbreviated as YR.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyra is a northern constellation, a group of stars containing Vega.

clue.text: One who represents us (in Havana?) after doctor's captured in battle

indicators.note: something captured is held inside, so the doctor goes within the phrase

parts.note: Greene's novel Our Man in Havana

explanation.surface: A spy story: our agent in Cuba follows a captured doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Our Man in Havana is a Graham Greene spy novel; MD goes after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Omdurman, near Khartoum, was where Kitchener's army fought the Mahdists in 1898.

clue.text: Ill-mannered actors get plastered

explanation.surface: Rude performers get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastered' looks like slang for drunk; it is the literal coating of a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: To roughcast a wall is to coat it with coarse plaster, so roughcast means plastered.

clue.text: Initially, laboratory imported aerosols after scientist missed mist in Asia Minor

indicators.note: what is missed is left out, so that word is taken away

parts.note: a scientist who studies body structure
taken as written, to be removed

indicators.note: only the opening letter of each word is wanted

parts.note: first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A lab's foreign sprays fail to reach a scientist working in Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatolia is the large peninsula of western Asia that forms most of modern Turkey.

clue.text: God holding ruler responsible for means of identification

indicators.note: holding something means keeping it inside, so the ruler sits within

explanation.surface: A deity and a monarch are blamed for how people are identified.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinctive patterns or symbols on an animal or object let one recognise it.

clue.text: Unprepossessing, lowly — extremely unpleasant

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only those are kept

explanation.surface: A description of someone plain and humble, and thoroughly disagreeable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unprepossessing' looks like the definition but is fodder; 'extremely' covers both words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly can describe a nasty situation or mood, so it works as a synonym for unpleasant.

clue.text: Stop going north and south

indicators.note: in a down light, reading upward or downward gives the same word

parts.note: the definition, whose answer reads identically both ways

explanation.surface: An instruction to halt travel in either direction.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a down clue, so north and south are up and down the column.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull up is to bring a vehicle to a halt, a common phrasal verb meaning stop.

clue.text: Major advance after interval is over

explanation.surface: A big step forward comes once the half-time pause is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakthrough is a sudden important discovery or progress.

clue.text: Characters in a pea-green boat go together

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters found inside the words that follow

parts.note: found across the middle of the compound

explanation.surface: The Owl and the Pussy-cat sail off in their pea-green boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The pea-green boat is from Edward Lear's poem The Owl and the Pussy-cat; 'boat' is only scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that agree match or harmonise, so they go well together.

clue.text: Injury caused by fire or running water

definitions.meaning: first meaning: damage to skin from heat
second meaning: a small stream, chiefly Scottish

explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland and northern England a burn is a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a wound from flames and a small flowing stream.

clue.text: A river between lakes and bay

indicators.note: what is between is flanked on both sides, so these letters go inside

explanation.surface: A geographical note: a river runs between lakes and a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay' looks like a coastal feature beside rivers and lakes; it is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay laurel is an evergreen tree whose leaves are used in cooking.

clue.text: Short distance and long distance combined

parts.note: an old measure of about three miles

explanation.surface: A short hop and a long journey put together.
explanation.definitionFit: Parties in league are allied or conspiring, joined together in a shared cause.

clue.text: Roman, for example. with kind expression

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman with a gentle look on his face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman' suggests a citizen of Rome; it is roman type, as opposed to italic.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman is the standard upright style of print, one example of a design of lettering.

clue.text: Just so in a film

explanation.surface: Something exactly right appears in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' suggests cinema; it is a thin surface layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A patina is a thin coating that forms on metal or wood with age.
